about.title: About the GRC
about.headline: We listen, we gather the numbers, and we bring them to the table.
about.description: The Graduate Representation Committee (GRC) is a group of graduate students who represent the interests of all graduate students in the University of Toronto Faculty of Medicine.

surveyFigure.statement: survey respondents said they draw on more than their stipend to cover living costs.
surveyFigure.source: From last year's GRC Finance and Living Survey (2025/26, 244 respondents).

purposeParagraphs: The GRC is dedicated to keeping you informed about important faculty and university policies that affect your graduate experience. We actively seek your feedback to ensure our advocacy aligns with your needs and sentiments.
about.objectivesIntro: Through our initiatives, we aim to ensure that you:

objectives.text: Are well-informed about policies and resources impacting your graduate life.
Feel heard and know that your opinions contribute to improving our graduate community.
Experience positive changes through our advocacy and policy efforts.

workParagraphs: The GRC primarily focuses on student stipends and the Faculty of Medicine Harmonized Base Funding Agreement (HBFA).

workSteps.title: Survey
workSteps.text: We conduct the GRC Finance and Living Survey to gather data on your finances, living conditions, career prospects, and well-being.

workSteps.title: Compare
workSteps.text: We combine this data with Statistics Canada metrics on Toronto's cost of living.

workSteps.title: Report
workSteps.text: The GRC Finance and Living Report highlights the realities of graduate student life.

workSteps.title: Recommend
workSteps.text: The report includes our recommendations for HBFA changes.

resourcesBand.text: You asked for one place to find every resource. This site is becoming that place.

about.contactPrompt: Questions, ideas or concerns about graduate life in the Faculty of Medicine?

members.name: Yumnah Jafri
members.bio: I am a second-year MSc student in Nutritional Sciences exploring the implementation of a combined community gardening and nutrition education program in Mississauga, Ontario. Through the GRC, I hope to strengthen outreach across departments and collaborate with the team to ensure that the perspectives of a diverse range of graduate students are meaningfully represented. In my free time, I enjoy reading and running.

members.name: Kattreen Hanna
members.bio: I am a PhD student in Laboratory Medicine and Pathobiology at the University of Toronto, where my research focuses on developing a cancer-on-chip model for kidney cancer to better understand tumour–immune interactions and support personalized treatment approaches. Outside of research, I enjoy travelling, exploring new places, trying new things, and staying involved in science communication and community events. I joined the GRC to contribute to a supportive graduate community and help amplify the voices and experiences of students across the Faculty of Medicine.

members.name: Ellie Yang
members.bio: Ellie is a PhD student in the Department of Medical Biophysics at the University of Toronto, where her research focuses on cancer nanomedicine and antitumour immune responses. She joined the GRC to help improve communication between graduate students and the Faculty and to support student engagement and advocacy. Outside of research, she enjoys contributing to student and community initiatives.

members.name: Michael Maddalena
members.bio: I am a fifth-year PhD student in the Department of Medical Biophysics. My research is primarily linked to radiation oncology, specifically focusing on advanced medical imaging techniques and computational approaches applied to neuroendocrine oncology. Outside of research, I mainly spend my time playing ice hockey, bouldering, and enjoying various board games.

members.name: Jia Du
members.bio: I'm a PhD student in the Buechler/Epelman Labs in the Department of Immunology. I study tissue inflammation in the context of ischemic heart injury. I enjoy running and playing volleyball outside of the lab. I joined the GRC to better understand graduate student needs and advocate for the overall well-being of my peers to FoM staff through evidence-based analysis.

members.name: Tianyi/Amanda Liu
members.bio: Amanda is a third-year PhD student in the Institute of Medical Science, where her research focuses on gene and environment interaction for bipolar disorder. Through GRC, she hopes to advocate for students’ voices and build better communication between graduate students and the faculty. Outside of research, she enjoys travelling and skiing.
